three years ago, when i first played persona 5, it was when i felt like my life was falling apart and i had nowhere to belong. this game gave me a place to belong even if it was fictional. futaba as a character mirrored me in so many ways that showed me that if she could belong somewhere, maybe i could again. 

the last week i replayed persona 5 royal, this time including the third semester since last time i didnt meet the requirements of confidants (oops).

now, i understand more of the themes and this time the game showed me that as long as i stay true to who i am and follow a path of my chosing, i will be okay and i will have somewhere to belong.

the ending hit so much harder for me this time seeing all the characters go off to do their own things since this time im the same age as them. 

this game has shown me that i can belong somewhere and that as long as i stay true to myself and follow the path i want, all will not be lost. persona 5 royal's 3rd semester in particular (alongside futaba's palace) showed me that i cant run away and hide from the bad things that have happened, no matter how hard it is to face.

also it has really great music and story and gameplay and characters and all that so play it please and thank you

This game is like a house of cards, every element is flimsy on it's own but when brought together they form a much greater whole. Unfortunately like a house of cards it falls apart easily, especially if you aren't the target audience, which I am not. I understand that characters being one dimensional and puzzles being too easy aren't necessarily problems for most people, but they are for me. I understand that most people don't care if the gameplay is a little boring or the story a bit repetitive but I do. I understand that this game is perfectly fine in many ways and that a lot of the problems I have with it are nitpicks, but with as many nitpicks as I have they become overwhelming every time I play. It was death by a thousand paper cuts; in the same way that the game forms a greater whole it's problems form a greater hole, and for me the problems with the game didn't outweigh it's virtues.

While it's definitely not my favourite Persona game, Royal is definitely a huge improvement from the original and surprisingly generous with additional content being bundled with the game's entire cost. It's a shame Atlus isn't as generous with Reload and now Revival which does make it clear that Persona 5 is their favourite of the Persona games. Royal at least polishes the gameplay and pretty much makes the core game a breeze to play through even if you ignore the DLC personas so it's very accessible for people getting into the series. I recommend going in blind on the first playthrough and going with the vanilla true ending then replaying the game on new game + and experience the Royal content while min-maxxing your team for the harder fights, but trying out the additional content on your first playthrough is alright you just miss out on a lot of touching moments if you haven't completed everything within the given time unless you follow a strict guide from day one, which then defeats the purpose of experiencing what the game has to offer and in general having fun. Goes on sale frequently so I'd suggest waiting before buying.

top 10 worst games i've ever played. it has a neat concept but butchers the execution in many ways. it has a number of neat moments, but characters become flat archetypes that don't actually fit what they were rather quickly, and in a game driven by its gameplay as much as its story, it's unfortunate that neither of its driving factors were its strengths. the ability to joker to bring anything he wants with him and the lack of ability to reliably know the typings of your future enemies means the optimal strategy is just to pick your favorite allies, who is plot relevant, and then have a team of balanced typings you can have joker call on. it becomes pokemon level rote memorization of type matchups and the most basic rock paper scissors matchups possible.  this system also brings up uneccessary ethical concerns narratively regarding the sentience of cognitions, shadows, whatever the specific enemies were called, i forget which exact name goes where. as these beings are said to just be mindless evil,  but apperantly can do things like bargain, and most notably beg for their lives, as well as be executed to be fused into new beings. with our cast who are meant to be heroes, not even sparing a thought to this as to justify it or understand why any of this should be ok. (to be clear i'm aware defending yourself isn't evil, rather if you are defending yourself and your opponent surrenders, normally a hero of all people would consider that time to spare  your enemy if possible, or recruit them, notably not executing them once they join you either). additionally the game is contradictory with its establishment of character, uses fanservice to justify a humiliating arc for a character to be effectively told by her subcontious that she likes to be seductive with people and forced to present herself in a sexual way until she complies (no other character works like this, every other character's persona and outfit is a representation of their liberation and comfort in being themselves), and the list goes on.

the game could have been better if it simply allowed anne to go on an arc to not be sexualized but be comfortable being viewed as attractive, if it forced joker to stay with his regular persona and used that as a method to build your persona's loadout or build in some way as well as using arsene to have story with joker, however the game deliberately strips your very cool unique persona from you, to force you to use the asset flops from SMT which are almost entirely recycled (or recycled from here to there, either way both games suck). 

the idea for the phantom thieves and personas are very cool ideas of worldbuilding, and the idea of a bunch of misfit teenagers learning that their rebellion isn't inherently wrong and can be good, within reason, is a neat idea. especially if it culminates in them facing a representation of the fear of the future/desire for order. the desire to create a perfect future and the costs that has to ensure, vs the trust you need to have in people and  yourself to live the life  you want, and be encouraged to do so in a way that encourages growth and achievement rather than directionless dreaming.  persona is a game of ideas, without the substance to back them up.

Persona 5 Royal was put straight into my top 5 games of all time. Persona is never going to be a game for everyone, it's pacing is slow, not everyone likes turn based combat (I am one of those people), and there is some themes that are less than desirable for most people. (Sexual themes, Sucide, Questionable Dating Choices.) But the story is absolutely incredible! The art direction is so pretty and inspiring to look at. I don't know if anyone has felt this, but have you ever been in the car at night and an absolute magestical song is playing on the radio or shuffles through your headphones, and that feeling of Ecstasy comes over you. That's what this game felt like for me! Absolute Cinema.
